title: Runbook: feedback threads & mini-proposal anchors (Apr 2026)
body:
Status & purpose:
This doc is a compact runbook for the customer-success triage team to translate recent customer threads (Apr 2026) into small, testable proposals and prioritized quick fixes. Not a final roadmap — meant to capture emergent patterns, low-friction experiments, and anchor owners for follow-up.

TL;DR highlights:
- Two persistent friction clusters: 1) token-cost visibility at route/model granularity; 2) fallthrough behavior when Dedicated capacity is tight (silent failures vs graceful downgrade).
- High-impact quick wins (<= 2 wk): add a token-cost drill-down to per-route console page; expose a clearer fallback log entry in API responses for failed reservations.
- Medium bets (1–3 months): small routing policy UI to define preferred fallback models + canned canary templates for Dedicated customers.
- Hypothesis: ~30% of churn risk for mid-market customers is driven by unpredictable billing spikes tied to batching defaults + lack of per-route attribution. Need validation via a short cohort experiment.

Source signals condensed (raw threads sampled):
- Thread A (Enterprise onboarding call): "We ran overnight load tests and woke up to a bill 4x our estimate — can't map tokens to product routes or user cohorts." (Customer: FinAnalytics)
- Thread B (Support ticket CS-4128): Dedicated pool fallback silently returned 503s during burst window; SDK retried but customer app logged unhelpful errors. "Why did our model suddenly degrade? No trace."
- Thread C (Customer Slack excerpt): "We want a button to pin a cheaper quantized variant for non-critical flows."
- Multiple mentions: desire for per-request / per-route sampling traces (cost + latency) and cheaper non-SLO tiers that are explicit, not implicit hacks.

Short-form vignettes (for product storytelling):
- "Night-run surprise": FinAnalytics set batching to default and used a 1024-seq test; token accounting came from aggregate metrics only — engineers couldn't map to feature flags or UI routes. Outcome: credit exhaustion and paused pipelines.
- "Silent fallback": RetailApp experienced Dedicated capacity preemption and saw 503 bursts; their front-end surfaced opaque errors and a costly retry loop. They'd prefer an automatic, documented downgrade to a compatible open model with a clear header telling them why.

Root-cause hypotheses (quick):
1) Observability gap: console aggregates mask per-route token churn — attribution missing at the route -> user cohort level.
2) UX gap: fallback behaviors exist in runtime but are not surfaced in call-level metadata or console alerts.
3) Economics gap: customers can't easily configure cost-aware model variants per route (dev vs prod).

Proposed small experiments / quick fixes (owners & rough estimate):
- Quick Win A: Add "per-route token breakdown" panel to Console Route view (mock + backend API + spike of telemetry). Owner: Jun Park (dev), ETA: 10 days. Impact: direct reduction of billing confusion.
- Quick Win B: API change to include fallback_reason and fallback_model_id in streaming headers when automatic routing/fallback occurs. Owner: Mateo Ruiz (serving), ETA: 5 days for spec + 2-week rollout behind feature flag. Impact: improves debugability and reduces opaque 503 handling. Linked ticket: JIRA:CS-4128.
- Quick Win C: Playbook snippet for SRE/Customer Success to run a "billing postmortem" template with customers (doc + checklist). Owner: Sofia Ramirez (CS ops), ETA: 3 days. Impact: immediate reduction in escalations.

Medium experiments (requires product + infra coordination):
- Experiment 1: Route-level cost-saver toggles (UI + SDK): let customers select a preferred fallback family (eg, quantized-x or open-small) per route; include estimated cost delta in UI. Owner: Product-Hosted-API, partner: Console eng. Duration: 6–12 weeks.
- Experiment 2: Canary rollout templates for Dedicated: UI to create canary policies (10% traffic to fallback, automatic metrics check). Owner: product/console, SRE review. Duration: 8 weeks.

Metrics to validate impact (start-of-experiment baseline to measure):
- Reduction in "billing surprise" escalations (tickets tagged billing-surprise) by 40% in the cohort.
- Time-to-resolution for Dedicated fallback incidents down from median 4 hrs to <1 hr with better headers/tracing.
- Adoption rate of route-level cost toggles in pilot accounts (>20% of targeted routes).

Open questions / unknowns:
- How much additional telemetry retention will be required for per-route attribution? (cost and infra impact)
- Any security/compliance implications of including fallback_reason in streaming headers for Private customers? Need sec sign-off.
- UX: how to surface cost estimates without causing analysis paralysis for customers? (We should experiment with a 1–2 line estimate + link to deeper analysis.)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: telemetry addition could increase egress/ingest costs. Mitigation: sample at 1% initially; add a console toggle for increased fidelity per-account.
- Risk: exposing fallback reasons leaks internal model names. Mitigation: map internal model ids to customer-visible aliases and provide opt-out.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Jun: mock console panel (per-route token breakdown) and share screenshot in #cs-product by 2026-04-30.
- Mateo: draft API header proposal (fallback_reason header) + minimal SDK patch for node/python by 2026-05-04.
- Sofia: assemble billing postmortem playbook doc and send to CS leads for feedback by 2026-04-30.
- Aisha (owner): run a 45-min sync with Product-Hosted-API and Serving runtime to align on feasibility and infra cost assumptions — schedule for week of 2026-05-03.

Notes to self (unpolished):
- Keep proposals modular: customers need option to opt into extra telemetry rather than forced ingestion.
- Consider small pilot with FinAnalytics + RetailApp for two different axis (billing attribution vs graceful fallback). Offer credits for pilot instrumentation.
- Cross-ref: Confluence page with raw quotes (confluence:CCS-FEEDBACK-2026-04) — I should pull 5 representative transcripts into the pilot packet.

References / tickets mentioned:
- Support ticket: CS-4128 (Dedicated fallback silent 503s)
- GitHub PR: redwood-console PR#298 (route detail prototype)
- Confluence working draft: CCS-FEEDBACK-2026-04

If anything: flag me in the #cs-product thread with the subject "runbook: feedback -> quick wins" and I will prioritize follow-up.
